items.stem: Which part of a plant makes the seeds?
options: The stem that holds the plant up

explain.why: The stem supports the plant and carries water. It does not make seeds.
The root takes in water and mineral salts. It does not make seeds.
The leaf makes food. It does not make seeds.

solution: The flower is the part that makes the seeds.

figure.alt: A potted plant in line art.

items.stem: What is one job of the fruit of a plant?
options: To protect the seeds as they grow inside it
To make food for the plant
To take in water for the plant
To hold the plant up in the wind

explain.why: Food is made by the leaves, not by the fruit.
Water is taken in by the roots, not by the fruit.
Holding the plant up is the job of the stem and roots.

solution: The fruit covers and protects the seeds while they grow.

figure.alt: A fruit cut open, showing its skin, the soft part and a large seed inside.

items.stem: In the picture of the chilli plant, part B contains the seeds. What is part B?

explain.why: The flower is the part that later turns into the fruit. It is not the part holding the seeds.
Leaves are flat and green and do not hold seeds.
The stem is the long part that holds up the plant. It does not hold seeds.

solution: The chilli is the fruit. The seeds are inside it.

figure.alt: A chilli plant in line art with a flower, a ripe chilli with seeds showing, a leaf and a stem, with four marked positions.

items.stem: Why do many flowers have bright petals?
options: To take in water for the plant from the soil
To attract insects to the flower
To make food for the plant

explain.why: Water is taken in by the roots, not by petals.
Food is made by the leaves, not the petals.
Holding the plant up is done by the stem, not by the petals.

solution: Bright petals attract insects that visit the flower.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half, showing its petals and the parts inside.

items.stem: What is the job of a seed?
options: To make food for the plant
To grow into a new plant
To take in water for the plant

explain.why: Food is made by the leaves, not by a seed.
Taking in water is the job of the roots.
Holding the leaves up is the job of the stem.

solution: A seed can grow into a new plant when it gets what it needs.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open, showing its outer covering and the parts inside.

items.stem: A farmer picks guavas from a tree. Which part of the plant is a guava?

explain.why: Seeds are found inside the guava. The whole guava is the fruit.
A guava starts as a flower, but the part we pick is the fruit.
Roots grow in the soil. A guava grows on the tree.

solution: A guava is a fruit, with seeds inside.

items.stem: Look at the picture of the flower cut in half. Which part is brightly coloured and attracts insects?

explain.why: Part B is inside the flower and makes pollen. It is not there to attract insects.
Part C is inside the flower. It receives pollen and is not the bright outer part.
Part D is at the base of the flower and later grows into the fruit.

solution: Part A is a petal. Bright petals attract insects.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half in line art, showing its petals and the parts inside, with four marked positions.

items.stem: Look at the picture of the bean seed cut open. Part A covers the outside of the seed. What is the job of part A?
options: To take in water and mineral salts for the young plant
To make food for the seed
To protect the parts inside the seed
To attract insects to the seed

explain.why: Water is taken in by the root of the young plant, not by the covering.
Seeds do not make food. Leaves make food once the plant grows.
Insects are attracted to the flower, not to the seed covering.

solution: The outer covering of a seed protects the parts inside.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open in line art, showing its outer covering and the parts inside, with three marked positions.

items.stem: The soft part of the mango (part A) is eaten by animals, which may drop the seed (part B) far away. How does this help the mango tree?
options: More leaves grow on the tree
The seeds are spread to new places far away
The roots take in more water
The flowers open earlier in the year

explain.why: Eating the fruit does not make more leaves grow.
Eating the fruit does not change how much water the roots take in.
Animals eating the fruit do not make flowers open earlier.

solution: Animals that eat the fruit spread the seeds to other places.

figure.alt: A mango cut open in line art, showing its skin, the soft part and a large seed inside, with three marked positions.

items.stem: In the picture of the flower cut in half, which part grows into the fruit after the flower has been pollinated?

explain.why: Part A is a petal. Petals attract insects and later fall off.
Part B makes pollen. It does not grow into the fruit.
Part C receives the pollen. It does not grow into the fruit.

solution: Part D is at the base of the flower. After pollination it grows into the fruit.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half in line art, showing its petals and the parts inside, with four marked positions.

items.stem: A bean seed is cut open. Which part gives the young plant food until its leaves can make food?
options: Both part A and part C

explain.why: Part A is the outer covering. It protects the seed and does not give food.
Part C is the young plant itself. It uses the food stored in the seed leaf (part B).
Part A protects the seed and part C is the young plant. Neither is the food store, which is part B.

solution: The food store in the seed (part B) feeds the young plant until its first leaves can make food.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open in line art, showing its outer covering and the parts inside, with three marked positions.

items.stem: Sara picks all the flowers from a chilli plant. What will the plant not be able to make?

explain.why: New leaves grow from the stem. They do not need flowers.
New roots grow from the roots already there. They do not need flowers.
New stems grow from the stem tips and do not need flowers.

solution: Fruits and seeds form from flowers, so without flowers no fruits form.

items.stem: A bean seed has its food store (part B) removed and is then planted. What is most likely to happen?
options: The young plant grows faster because it has less to carry
The young plant makes seeds sooner
The young plant gets food from its seed coat instead
The young plant grows poorly with less food

explain.why: The food store feeds the young plant, so it grows poorly without it.
A young plant with less food would not make seeds sooner.
The seed coat protects the seed and does not provide food.

solution: The food store feeds the young plant until its leaves can make food.
Without it, the young plant has far less food.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open in line art, showing its outer covering and the parts inside, with three marked positions.

items.stem: Which row about the flower, fruit and seed is correct?
options: Flower: protects seeds; fruit: makes seeds; seed: makes food
Flower: grows into a plant; fruit: makes seeds; seed: protects the fruit
Flower: makes seeds; fruit: protects them; seed: grows into a plant
Flower: makes food; fruit: grows into a plant; seed: makes seeds

explain.why: Flowers make seeds and fruits protect them. Seeds do not make food.
Seeds grow into plants and do not protect the fruit.
Leaves make food, and a fruit does not grow into a plant. A seed does.

solution: The flower makes the seeds.
The fruit protects the seeds.
A seed can grow into a new plant.

items.stem: What is the movement of pollen from one flower to another called?

explain.why: Germination is when a seed starts to grow into a young plant.
Seed dispersal is the spreading of seeds away from the parent plant.
Fertilisation is when a male and a female cell join. It happens after pollination.

solution: Moving pollen from one flower to another is called pollination.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half, showing its petals and the parts inside.

items.stem: Which of these animals often carry pollen from flower to flower?

explain.why: Worms and snails stay low on the ground and do not visit flowers to feed.
Fish and frogs live in or near water, not among flowers.
These stay mostly on the ground or in the soil.

solution: Bees and butterflies visit flowers for the sweet nectar, so pollen sticks to them and is carried on.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half, showing its petals and the parts inside.

items.stem: Which of these things must a bean seed have to start growing?

explain.why: A seed does not need light, soil or wind to start growing.
These are not needed for a seed to germinate.
A seed needs none of these to begin to grow.

solution: A seed needs water, air and warmth to germinate.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open, showing its outer covering and the parts inside.

items.stem: What do we call it when a seed starts to grow into a young plant?

explain.why: Pollination is the movement of pollen between flowers.
Fertilisation is the joining of a male and a female cell inside the flower.
Seed dispersal is the spreading of seeds.

solution: A seed starting to grow is germination.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open, showing its outer covering and the parts inside.

items.stem: In the picture of the bean seed cut open, part C is the tiny young plant inside. What will part C grow into?
options: The fruit that holds the seeds
The food store of the seed

explain.why: The covering is part A and does not grow into the new plant.
A fruit forms from the flower, not from the young plant inside the seed.
The food store is a different part (part B).

solution: Part C is the young plant, or baby plant, inside the seed.
It grows into a new plant.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open in line art, showing its outer covering and the parts inside, with three marked positions.

items.stem: What do we call the carrying of seeds away from the parent plant?

explain.why: Germination is when a seed starts to grow.
Pollination is the movement of pollen.
Fertilisation is the joining of a male and a female cell.

solution: Carrying seeds away from the parent plant is called seed dispersal.

items.stem: Why is it good for a plant to have its seeds carried far away from it?
options: The seeds can make food for the parent plant
The parent plant can make more flowers
The young plants have more room and light
The seeds can grow into fruits right away

explain.why: Seeds do not make food for the parent plant.
Where seeds land does not change how many flowers the parent makes.
Seeds do not become fruits. They grow into new plants.

solution: Seeds that fall next to the parent must share its light, water and space.
Seeds carried far away have more room to grow.

items.stem: Which of these seeds is carried away by the wind?

explain.why: A coconut is spread by water, not wind.
A burr has hooks, so it is carried on animals' fur.
A mango is a juicy fruit. Animals eat it and spread the seed.

solution: A dandelion seed has light hairs that catch the wind and carry it away.

items.stem: Which of these seeds is carried away by water?
options: A seed with a light wing
A seed in a bright red berry

explain.why: A winged seed is carried by wind.
A hooked seed is carried on animals' fur.
A bright berry is eaten by animals, which spread the seed.

solution: A coconut has a thick husk that floats, so water can carry it away.

items.stem: Birds eat red berries and later drop the seeds in their droppings far away. How are the seeds spread?

explain.why: The seeds are carried inside the bird, not blown by wind.
Water does not carry the seeds in this case.
The fruit is eaten. It does not split open to throw the seeds out.

solution: Animals eat the fruit and drop the seeds somewhere else, so the seeds are spread by animals.

items.stem: The ripe fruits of a rubber tree dry in the sun and burst with a snap. The seeds land far from the tree. How are the seeds spread?

explain.why: Wind does not throw the seeds. The fruit bursts by itself.
No animal is needed. The fruit bursts open by itself.
The fruits dry in the sun. Water is not involved.

solution: Some fruits dry and burst open, which throws the seeds away from the plant.

items.stem: Which of these plants makes spores instead of seeds?

explain.why: A hibiscus makes flowers and seeds.
A mango tree makes flowers, fruits and seeds.
A bean plant makes flowers, pods and seeds.

solution: Ferns do not make flowers or seeds.
They make tiny spores.

items.stem: A gardener pushes a cut branch of a rose bush into wet soil. Weeks later it has roots and leaves and is a new rose plant. What did the new plant grow from?
options: A part of the old plant
A seed hidden inside the branch
A fruit of the old plant

explain.why: No seed was planted. The branch itself grew roots and leaves.
A fruit was not planted, only the cut branch.
Pollen does not grow into a plant by itself.

solution: A new plant can grow from a cut piece of stem.
No seed was planted.

items.stem: Pollen is made in the male part of a flower called the ____.

explain.why: Petals attract insects. They do not make pollen.
The ovary is the female part. It holds the tiny egg cells that become seeds.
The stalk holds up the flower. It does not make pollen.

solution: The stamen is the male part of the flower and makes pollen.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half, showing its petals and the parts inside.

items.stem: After a flower has been pollinated and fertilised, which part of it grows into the fruit?

explain.why: The petals usually wither and fall off.
The stamen makes pollen. It does not become the fruit.
The stalk holds up the flower and does not become the fruit.

solution: The ovary holds the tiny egg cells.
After fertilisation, it grows into the fruit and the egg cells become seeds.

items.stem: A bean seed is planted in soil. Where does the young plant get its food before its leaves can make food?
options: From the food stored in the seed

explain.why: Soil gives water and mineral salts, but not food.
Air alone cannot feed a young plant that has no leaves yet.
Sunlight is only used by leaves to make food, and there are no leaves yet.

solution: A bean seed has a food store inside it.
The young plant uses this until its leaves can make food.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open, showing its outer covering and the parts inside.

items.stem: Which of these must happen first before a flower can make seeds?
options: The seeds are spread by wind

explain.why: Seeds are spread only after they have been made.
Growing from a seed happens after the seed has been made.
The fruit forms only after pollination, so this comes later.

solution: Seeds can form only after pollen reaches the female part of a flower.
Spreading and growing of seeds come later.

figure.alt: A flower cut in half, showing its petals and the parts inside.

items.stem: A bean seed is put on dry cotton wool in a warm room. After a week it has not started to grow. What is missing?

explain.why: A seed can start to grow without soil, for example on wet cotton wool.
A seed does not need light to start to grow.
Wind is not needed for a seed to start to grow.

solution: A seed needs water, air and warmth to germinate.
The room is warm and has air. The cotton wool is dry, so water is missing.

figure.alt: A bean seed cut open, showing its outer covering and the parts inside.
